01.r: Places Judas after the man just mentioned.

02.r: The leader mentioned just before Judas.

03.r: Judas came forward as a leader.
03.n: Abbott-Smith classes the second aorist, the form here, as intransitive: to rise, not to raise. The BSB's 'appeared' is a looser rendering.

04.r: The man who led the revolt.
04.n: Abbott-Smith notes that the Greek name is the same as Judah, the son of Jacob.

05.r: Marks 'Galilean' as a title identifying this Judas.

06.n: An adjective used as a noun, 'the Galilean'. The KJV, Geneva, DRC and ASV turn it into 'of Galilee'.

07.r: Sets the time of the revolt.

10.r: The article; 'of' comes from the genitive case of the noun.

11.r: The official listing of people, named here to date the revolt.
11.n: Abbott-Smith gives, for late writers, 'a register, enrolment, census'; it is the noun of the verb 'to register' used in Luke 2:3, on this page. This study renders it 'registration' to keep it apart from κῆνσος, 'census tax'. The KJV's 'taxing' and the Geneva's 'tribute' name a payment, which the word itself does not.

13.r: He led people away into revolt.
13.n: Abbott-Smith gives the transitive sense 'to put away, lead away', and for this verse 'metaphorically, to move to revolt'.

14.r: Those Judas drew to his cause.
14.n: The word has no article and no number: simply 'people'. The KJV's 'much people' comes from an extra word in its Greek text (see the note on the Textus Receptus).

18.r: Judas, like the leader before him, came to nothing.
18.n: A contraction of καί and ἐκεῖνος, literally 'and that one'; Abbott-Smith gives 'and he' and 'he also'. The YLT keeps the literal form.

19.r: Judas was killed or came to ruin.
19.n: The middle voice of the verb that, in the active, means to destroy utterly. The verse does not say how he perished.

20.r: Joins the fate of his followers.

21.r: Every one of his followers, without exception.

22.r: Defines 'all' as everyone who followed him.

23.r: They had been won over to Judas and were following his lead.
23.n: The verb is the passive of 'persuade', in the imperfect: literally 'were being persuaded by him', that is, they were listening to him and following. The YLT keeps the imperfect with 'were obeying'.

25.r: His movement broke up and its members went their own ways.
25.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'to scatter abroad, disperse' and lists this verse under its use of persons. In Matthew 25:24, on this page, the same verb is used of winnowing grain.

tr_note: The Textus Receptus adds ἱκανόν, 'a considerable number', before 'people'. That is the source of 'much people' in the KJV, Geneva and YLT; the critical text reads only 'people'.
